name: Vivarium — Geneware Social & Display Net
description: Vivarium is the dominant platform for geneware expression, where users document, rate, and discuss their cosmetic and functional genetic modifications in real-time visual feeds and tagged body-catalogues. Founded in 2209 by geneware artist Priya-Solène Adichie-Marchetti out of a converted grow-lab in the Tier 3 Lakeview Stack, it began as a space for modification journaling but rapidly became a cultural force defining what bodies mean in 2220s Meridian. Signature features include 'Before/After/Becoming' triple-timeline posts, live molt-documentation for users mid-modification cycle, and the controversial 'Lineage Tag' system that traces which geneware aesthetics inspired which. Corporate geneware firms now pay aggressively for sponsored body-logs from high-follower users, creating a new class of 'flesh influencer.'
cultural_impact: Vivarium has made geneware modification aspirational across Tiers 2 and 3, normalizing bioluminescent skin, decorative horns, and patterned fur as everyday aesthetics rather than fringe statements. Its trending tags directly influence what modification clinics stock and what geneware designs get fast-tracked by manufacturers.
key_figures: Dr. Nkechi Vasquez-Holm (geneware ethicist and frequent platform critic)
locations: The Dermis — a Vivarium-sponsored IRL gallery in Midway Concourse
story_hooks: A user's 'Lineage Tag' inadvertently proves a major corponation stole a geneware design from a Shelf artist — and the platform is pressured to scrub the evidence.

A black-market geneware modification goes catastrophically wrong on a live molt-documentation stream, and the footage is both evidence of corporate negligence and the most-viewed post in platform history.
Tómas Yuen-Abara's sponsored posts have been subtly altering his followers' body-image BCI feedback loops — and someone just found the code buried in a sponsored tag.
user_base: Approximately 11 million active users; primarily Tier 2-3, ages 17-35, with significant Tier 4 lurker population
monetization: Sponsored body-logs, geneware clinic partnerships, modification clinic referral fees, premium 'Vivarium Verified Body' certification subscriptions
notable_feature: The 'Becoming' timeline — a continuous living document of a user's modification journey that updates automatically via BCI-linked biometric tracking, showing real-time physiological changes as geneware integrates
